entries.title: Proverbs 26:1
segments: ¶As snow in summer and rain in harvest, So honor is not fitting for a fool.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:2
segments: ¶Like a flitting sparrow, like a flying swallow, So a curse without cause shall not alight.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:3
segments: ¶A whip for the horse, A bridle for the donkey, And a rod for the fool's back.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:4
segments: ¶Do not answer a fool according to his folly, Lest you also be like him.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:5
segments: Answer a fool according to his folly, Lest he be wise in his own eyes.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:6
segments: ¶He who sends a message by the hand of a fool Cuts off [his own] feet [and] drinks violence.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:7
segments: [Like] the legs of the lame that hang limp [Is] a proverb in the mouth of fools.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:8
segments: Like one who binds a stone in a sling [Is] he who gives honor to a fool.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:9
segments: [Like] a thorn [that] goes into the hand of a drunkard [Is] a proverb in the mouth of fools.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:10
segments: ¶The great [God] who formed everything Gives the fool [his] hire and the transgressor [his] wages.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:11
segments: ¶As a dog returns to his own vomit, [So] a fool repeats his folly.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:12
segments: ¶Do you see a man wise in his own eyes? [There is] more hope for a fool than for him.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:13
segments: ¶The lazy [man] says, "[There is] a lion in the road! A fierce lion [is] in the streets!"

entries.title: Proverbs 26:14
segments: ¶[As] a door turns on its hinges, So [does] the lazy [man] on his bed.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:15
segments: ¶The lazy [man] buries his hand in the bowl; It wearies him to bring it back to his mouth.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:16
segments: ¶The lazy [man is] wiser in his own eyes Than seven men who can answer sensibly.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:17
segments: ¶He who passes by [and] meddles in a quarrel not his own [Is like] one who takes a dog by the ears.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:18
segments: ¶Like a madman who throws firebrands, arrows, and death,

entries.title: Proverbs 26:19
segments: [Is] the man [who] deceives his neighbor, And says, "I was only joking!"

entries.title: Proverbs 26:20
segments: ¶Where [there is] no wood, the fire goes out; And where [there is] no talebearer, strife ceases.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:21
segments: [As] charcoal [is] to burning coals, and wood to fire, So [is] a contentious man to kindle strife.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:22
segments: The words of a talebearer [are] like tasty trifles, And they go down into the inmost body.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:23
segments: ¶Fervent lips with a wicked heart [Are like] earthenware covered with silver dross.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:24
segments: ¶He who hates, disguises [it] with his lips, And lays up deceit within himself;

entries.title: Proverbs 26:25
segments: When he speaks kindly, do not believe him, For [there are] seven abominations in his heart;

entries.title: Proverbs 26:26
segments: [Though his] hatred is covered by deceit, His wickedness will be revealed before the assembly.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:27
segments: ¶Whoever digs a pit will fall into it, And he who rolls a stone will have it roll back on him.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:28
segments: ¶A lying tongue hates [those who are] crushed by it, And a flattering mouth works ruin.
